newsitem.title: USA: One killed as tornadoes hit Alabama, Tennessee.
newsitem.headline: One killed as tornadoes hit Alabama, Tennessee.

text.p: Tornadoes that whipped through central Alabama and Tennessee late Friday killed at least one person while toppling trees, ripping off roofs and rupturing gas lines, authorities said Saturday.

In Tuscaloosa, Ala., Dr. Lyman Findley was killed when a tree fell on the pick-up truck he was sitting in. At least 10 other people were treated for minor injuries, Herman Gocke, nursing supervisor at Northport Hospital, said .

The tornado also ripped at residential homes and shops in a strip mall in the east of the city. "Right now we're in the process of assessing the number of homes damaged," said Don DeJarnette of the Tuscaloosa County Emergency Management Agency.
"Preliminary reports are that we have about 50 houses and businesses damaged but that's being revised," he said. "I wouldn't be surprised to see that reach 100."

In and around Murfreesboro, Tenn., about 30 miles (50 km) south of Nashville, about 20 people were treated for minor injuries. Hundreds more were left homeless after the tornadoes damaged or destroyed about 250 homes.
Rescue crews were still working to free people from damaged buildings in the nearby Barfield area of Rutherford County.

"So far we have had no confirmed fatalities, which is fantastic considering the velocity of these storms and the speed with which they moved through," said Cecil Whaley, head of the Tennessee Emergency Management Agency.
At least eight tornadoes tore through an eight-county area south of Nashville late Friday, police and emergency officials said.

Although Tuscaloosa was hardest hit by the tornado in Alabama, at least 29 homes in six other counties in the central part of the state were badly damaged, said Susan Morris of the American Red Cross in Birmingham.
Tuscaloosa resident Donna Roberts was driving home from her job at a car supply store when the tornado touched down.
"It was just a black bank of clouds when I saw the funnel come out," she said. She pulled over the car and lay across the front seat as a safety measure.
The Food World grocery store at the strip mall was almost completely destroyed, she said. More than a dozen cars were ruined, either tossed around by the winds or smashed by flying shopping carts.
"One car was actually picked up out of the parking lot and put down in the store in the cookie aisle," Robertson said.
In Tennessee, many of the hardest hit areas were rural and difficult to reach Saturday because roads were blocked by debris, said Whaley.
Electric power was reported to be out in Smyrna, site of a large Nissan plant, and homeward-bound motorists had been caught in huge traffic jams.
"We have broken gas lines to contend with, to avoid secondary explosions from that," Whaley said.
The Tennessee tornadoes also rolled through Wilson, Lincoln and Bedford counties, he said.
Rutherford County was hardest hit, sustaining about 75 percent of the damage in the eight-county area, said TEMA's Whaley.
